company_name: First Interstate BancSystem Inc. Common Stock (DE)
title: First Interstate and Centennial Youth Foundation Award $25,000 to Local Nonprofits
summary: First Interstate and the Centennial Youth Foundation awarded $25,000 to 11 nonprofits supporting youth programs in Yellowstone County.
body_markdown:
Eleven nonprofits received grants to expand educational, cultural, athletic, and social service opportunities for young people in Yellowstone County.


Supporting Yellowstone County Youth


First Interstate and the Centennial Youth Foundation awarded a combined $25,000 to 11 Yellowstone County nonprofits during a Nov. 5 ceremony in Billings.


The grants will support programs that help local youth learn, participate, build connections, and access essential services.


First Interstate established the Centennial Youth Foundation in 1982 during Billings’ centennial year. The Foundation provides grants to organizations and activities that create athletic, cultural, educational, and social service opportunities for youth in Yellowstone County.


“Today, we proudly continue that mission by investing in the nonprofit and community partners who make these opportunities possible,” said Brian Brown, Eastern Montana State President at First Interstate. “Congratulations to our 2026 grant recipients. We are grateful for your dedication to strengthening our communities and empowering the next generation of leaders. Your work continues to create a lasting impact on the youth and families of Yellowstone County.”


Meet the 2026 Grant Recipients


The Centennial Youth Foundation awarded grants to:


- Friendship House of Christian Services: $3,000
- Montana Rescue Mission: $3,000
- Yellowstone CASA: $3,000
- Education Foundation for Billings Public Schools: $2,500
- Billings Family YMCA: $2,500
- CLDI: $2,500
- Family Service: $2,000
- Billings Clinic Foundation: $2,000
- Yellowstone Art Museum: $2,000
- Girl Scouts of Montana and Wyoming: $1,950
- Chinook Horses: $550


Creating More Opportunities for Local Youth


Each recipient helps address a need or create an opportunity for young people in Yellowstone County. Together, their programs support education, family stability, creative expression, physical activity, mentorship, and community connection.


The Centennial Youth Foundation reflects First Interstate’s long-term commitment to the Billings community. By investing in organizations with local knowledge and direct community relationships, the Foundation helps more young people access programs and support close to home.


Learn more about First Interstate’s community investments in our[Community Scorecard](https://www.firstinterstatebank.com/company/commitment/community-scorecard) .
